Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# task-d58c8399: fill enclosed cavities

## When to Use
Use for recurring task id `task-d58c8399`, where color-6 outline segments enclose background regions and the fill color is 4.

## Validated rule
For task id `task-d58c8399`, color 6 forms outlined, axis-aligned shapes on a color-9 background. Recolor the enclosed interior/background cells bounded by those outlines to color 4. Keep the original color-6 outline cells and all other cells unchanged.

Confirmed by a demo with a narrow enclosed cavity between two vertical color-1 rails capped by horizontal segments, whose interior cells changed from background 0 to color 4, and a held-out correct submission. The test included two enclosed cavities inside color-6 outlines; their interior cells were filled with 4.

## Procedure
1. Identify bounded pockets of background color that are fully enclosed by the outline in the grid (4-neighbor connectivity); do not treat open gaps connected to the exterior as cavities.
2. Recolor only the interior background cells of those enclosed pockets to 4.
3. Preserve all outline cells and any exterior background or unrelated cells.
4. Verify grid dimensions and all row lengths before emitting the task's required action JSON.

## Evidence and limits
A demo and multiple correct held-out submissions validate the enclosed-cavity interpretation for this task ID. The demo's outline color was 1 and background 0; tests have used outline 1/background 5 and outline 6/background 9, with the same output fill color 4. A confirmed geometry was a 3x4 pocket: a top and bottom horizontal outline, vertical sides, and an extra horizontal ray extending outward from a side; fill only the 12 interior cells, preserving the ray and all outline. Another test had enclosed cavities in a wider shape. A later 26x12 test used outline 9 and field 1: a 2-cell vertical cavity between the split horizontal outline at row 4 and the lower horizontal cap, at column 8 (1-based), was filled with 4; the long downward 9-ray below the shape remained unchanged. This was confirmed correct. A 29x19 test used outline 7 and field 1 and had two separate enclosed cavities: a 2x4 pocket (rows 19-20, columns 5-8, 1-based) and a 4x2 pocket (rows 19-22, columns 17-18), both filled with 4; all exterior field cells remained 1. This submission was confirmed correct. Another confirmed 20x10 recurrence used outline 7 and field 6, with an enclosed 3x3 field pocket at rows 15-17, columns 7-9 (1-based); fill those nine cells with 4, preserving all exterior 6 cells and the 7 outline. A further correct 9x23 recurrence used outline 2 and background 0: the enclosure was a 3x2 cavity at rows 3-5, columns 5-6 (1-based), bounded by outline rows/columns and attached to an outward horizontal ray; recolor those six cells to 4 and preserve exterior background and all outline.
